messages.author: 63ddbb8fb7d057f7
messages.subject: comparability with brain connectivity toolbox
parts:
Hi Chris, 

thank you for creating this great package and providing such amazing support. 

After running the first analyses of my structural connectomics dataset (weighted undirected, FA) in the BCT in MATLAB, I came a cross the mtpc approach and thus your powerful package. To use the implementation of the mtpc in your package in R, I'm trying to transfer my previous analyses to brainGraph. 

So far it worked out fine and I was able to replicate and confirm the first results.

E.g. Left - Results of BCT for global efficiency with Eglob = efficiency_wei(W) (red patients, blue controls; dots and dashed line indicate thresholds at which significant group differences were found): Right - results of brainGraph with E.global.wt and corresponding mtpc results




However, for average local efficiency and clustering coefficient I'm not sure whether the BCT functions have a direct correlate in brainGraph? 


For average local efficiency I used: Eloc = efficiency_wei(W,2) in BCT (which seems to be an updated version of the original (Wang Y et al. (2016) Neural Comput 21:1-19.). Does this directly correspond to the E.local.wt attribute? The results are off by a few decimal points. 


For the clustering coefficient (clustering_coef_wu(W) in BCT) I'm not sure whether the corresponding measure in brainGraph should be 'transitivity' or 'Cp'? Both give different results.  




Thank you, Maria

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] comparability with brain connectivity toolbox
parts:
Hi Maria, thank you for the kind words. I am glad you have found the package useful.

The results for weighted global efficiency appear to be the same, as you noted.
Regarding weighted local efficiency and weighted clustering, "igraph" does not calculate weighted clustering in the same way. The transitivity is different, and igraph's weighted version -- transitivity(g, type='weighted') -- is also a different metric.
Since I wrote "efficiency", I simply use the 'original" equation and not any of the generalizations in Wang 2016. I would have to update the function but that is not on my to-do list for the near future. I can look more into those generalizations but I don't have a timeline for it.

If you are concerned about the similarity between BCT and brainGraph, I suggest first seeing if the values have high correlation between the two packages, and second see if they preserve any group differences (or lack thereof).

Chris

messages.author: 28bb28f8fe8898a5
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] comparability with brain connectivity toolbox
parts:
Unfortunately, back when I did that I wasn't good at keeping a detailed record
of it. I am sure that it was *unweighted*, and I would guess it was either
(where "g" is the graph of interest):

1. transitivity(g, type='localaverage') # Graph-level
2. transitivity(g) # Graph-level
3. transitivity(g, type='local', isolates='zero') # Vertex-level

My best guess is that it would be #1 above.

Chris
